A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FGAIF by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FGAIF benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative comparisons in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds feedback-label accuracy measurements, robustness evaluations, and alternative-feedback-model experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 removes the leading minus sign from the combined token-reward formula, changing the written reward specification. The three-stage pipeline, reward classifiers, and losses otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this formula revision changed the implementation; the expanded PPO and sentence-splitting descriptions are additional documentation.

E1.justification: The original MSCOCO training coverage and benchmark suite remain. Section 5.3 adds reward-model evaluation on Foggy images and longer responses containing 15–20 sub-segments. These extend domain and input-length coverage without changing the principal vision-language tasks.

E2.justification: The baseline membership in Tables 1–6 is unchanged. Appendices E and G add component-level comparisons using InternVL 2.5 (26B) instead of the LLaVA labeler and GPT-4o instead of GPT-3.5 for atomic-fact generation, including a separately evaluated FGAIF variant in Table 7.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols and training budgets are retained, but v2 substantially expands the evaluation design: manual binary-label assessment using 90 COCO images, reward-model accuracy comparisons involving 500 original and 200 longer-response samples, and testing on 200 Foggy images. Appendices E and G also introduce alternative-feedback-model experiments and a 10-example atomic-fact overlap assessment.

E4.justification: Beyond the unchanged component-removal and coarse-reward ablations, v2 adds response-length and distribution-shift robustness tests, manual feedback-quality validation, and InternVL/GPT-4o substitution studies. Appendix B adds labeler error cases, while Appendix H adds qualitative examples examining co-occurrence hallucinations. These substantially broaden analysis of the pipeline's reliability.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's disclosure of deterministic decoding settings does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results. Newly reported findings include reward-model accuracies of 80.4% on the original test set, 79.2% on longer responses, and 76% on Foggy images; labeler accuracies of 85.07% for LLaVA and 89.47% for InternVL; and Table 7's InternVL-feedback variant scoring 84.3 POPE F1 versus 83.4 for retained FGAIF. Appendix G additionally reports GPT-4o-based POPE F1 of 83.5 and 98% atomic-fact overlap. These are additional experimental results, not improvements to unchanged-setting entries in the original tables.

T1.justification: The reward definition in Section 4.3 changes sign without an accompanying explanation of equivalence. v2 also explicitly presents advantage estimation, value targets, and PPO optimization objectives in Section 4.3 and Appendix C. No theorem, proof, or new theoretical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: automated fine-grained hallucination labeling, three specialized reward models, PPO-based alignment, and effective hallucination reduction with a smaller policy model. Additional validation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of imperfect feedback, noise propagation through reward training and RL, generalization to longer and shifted inputs, and dependence on feedback-model quality. It also interprets object-existence rewards as especially important, discusses co-occurrence-driven errors, and argues that parallel reward models limit overhead. Section 5.2 narrows one performance statement from 'all' to 'most' metrics.

D1.justification: v2 adds PPO pseudocode, spaCy-plus-punctuation splitting details, feedback-model size, and decoding settings. Hardware, optimization settings, and training sample counts are retained and relocated. The release statement changes from code and parameters to code at a different repository location. Model-version disclosure is inconsistent: Section 5.1 specifies gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, whereas Appendix D specifies gpt-3.5-turbo-0125.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations covering multi-objective alignment, PPO/generalized advantage estimation, and newer hallucination evaluation and mitigation work. These broaden supporting context without substantially changing the positioning against coarse-grained human-feedback alignment. The FaithScore reference's publication update is a matched work, not a new research contribution.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: prompt material and experimental settings move from appendices into the main text, related work receives numbered subsections, and contributions and ablations become lists. PPO exposition and a Discussion subsection are added, and the appendices are reorganized around detailed results, implementation, errors, and analyses. Much of the original prose remains.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redrawn, including a visualized hallucinated scene and a redesigned pipeline schematic. Existing prompt figures move into the methodology, and the original qualitative comparison is retained as Figure 5. v2 adds error-case Figure 6, qualitative Figure 7, Table 7, and Algorithm 1, alongside journal-wide typography and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves validation of the central AI-feedback mechanism through manual accuracy checks, robustness tests, and alternative-labeler experiments, while adding useful implementation explanations. The gain is limited by unresolved reporting problems: conflicting ChatGPT versions, an unexplained reward-sign revision, and new Table 7 reporting LLaVA-7B FaithScore values of 89.3/71.1 that conflict with Table 3's 88.9/72.3. The additions strengthen the paper, but do not establish a substantial overall improvement.
